newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT slide in morning on newspaper report.
newsitem.headline: NTT slide in morning on newspaper report.

text.p: Shares in Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) slipped on Wednesday morning, the first decline in five days, on a newspaper report which said the government may sell its state-owned NTT shares as early as next spring.
A Ministry of Finance official later denied the report.
As of 0200 GMT, the shares were down 10,000 yen to 902,000.
Turnover totalled 13,607 shares as of 0200 GMT.
Profit-taking emerged after the Japanese daily Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun reported that the government was likely to sell some NTT shares as early as the April-June quarter, traders said.
NTT first went public in 1987, but the government still owns 65 percent of its shares. It planned to sell 500,000 NTT shares in the current year to March 1997, but has sold none of these so far.
The report was later denied by a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official, who said the ministry had not decided yet whether it would sell any state-owned NTT shares next business year.
"The article is pure speculation. We have not yet decided on any policy on further sales of state-owned NTT shares," the official told Reuters.
He said the ministry was closely watching stock market conditions before making any decision on the sales.

Asked about possible NTT share sales in 1997/98, the official said talks were underway between government ministries on how to draft next year's state budget, which would set the limit on how many NTT shares the government could sell in the year. "We cannot set any policy on next year's NTT share sales before the 1997/98 budget is completed," he said.
